attacksRun.attack: the Date field reads 2026-08-21 but the draft was authored on 2026-08-22 — every other draft in the wave matches its authoring date, so this one is stale
attacksRun.detail: Raised as a candidate SHOULD-FIX and it is the only measured divergence found in the entry. The divergence is real: the wave ran from 22:25 to 23:51 on 2026-08-21 with every sampled draft's Date field matching its authoring date, while this draft was written at 00:03 on 2026-08-22 and carries 2026-08-21. Three things defeat the finding. First, the protocol does not define the Date field as an authoring date; where COORD entries elaborate it at all they write 'Date: opened 2026-08-13', so the field carries the date the decision cycle was OPENED, and a cycle opened before midnight is accurately labelled 2026-08-21. Second, the adoption date is carried separately and authoritatively by the Status line, which adopted entries stamp as 'ADOPTED <date>' at adoption time; the operative date for the record is therefore not this field. Third, a filesystem mtime records when bytes were last written, not when content was composed, so it cannot establish that the cycle opened after midnight. Nothing in the entry's scope, pins, span, counts or status tokens depends on the field.
